categoryNote: Security protections stay ON by default (directive Section 15; SECURITY_POLICY.md Section 1). Eight entries are read-only reports (001, 002, 005, 006, 007, 009, 012, 015) and carry no mutation surface at all. Mutating entries are limited to changes that never reduce protection: documented UAC levels with EnableLUA=1 and the secure desktop always on (003), documented SmartScreen Warn/Block levels (004), Memory Integrity enablement behind ExplicitConsent with driver-compatibility gates (008), Controlled Folder Access enablement/audit plus per-app allow-listing (010), per-process exploit-mitigation increases (011), Windows Sandbox provisioning (013) and an explicitly consented virtualization-platform toggle with mandatory WSL2/Docker warnings (014). 003, 004 and 010 are additionally presetExcluded because they express security-posture choices whose Windows defaults already apply - a preset must never move a security setting on the owner's behalf. Disabling Defender, Firewall, UAC, SmartScreen, Secure Boot, TPM, VBS/Memory Integrity, Credential Guard, BitLocker, mitigation masks or the vulnerable-driver blocklist is NOT implemented anywhere in this category - those are the reference-ecosystem teardowns rejected in docs/RESEARCH_RECONCILIATION.md (Atlas/ReviOS/AME fallout, r2/r6). OWNERSHIP: the generic optional-feature mechanism is NX01-015 (reused, never duplicated); BCD/mitigation-mask/HPET work is NX17 territory and is never written here; Defender service/task changes are NX11/NX13 territory - NX14 reads state only. Banned-target guard: every NX14 registry writer calls Test-Nx14BannedRegistryTarget, a code-level mirror of registry/schema.json bannedRegistryTargets, so a banned write fails even if a future edit bypasses the static validator. Evidence: E1 entries cite only verified Microsoft Learn/support URLs (HTTP-verified 2026-11-23); the few decoded enum values that Microsoft does not publish are labeled as E0 observations with provenance in the report output.

tweaks.name: Defender status & health report
tweaks.description: Read-only report of Microsoft Defender Antivirus service state, protection features, signature age and policy preferences.
tweaks.objective: Establish what Defender actually reports before any NEXTRIX decision, without touching Defender configuration.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implements Get-Nx14DefenderStatusReport (src/nxcore/functions/NX14.ps1). Calls the documented Get-MpComputerStatus and Get-MpPreference cmdlets and reports a bounded, fixed property set: AntivirusEnabled, RealTimeProtectionEnabled, BehaviorMonitorEnabled, IoavProtectionEnabled, OnAccessProtectionEnabled, AMServiceEnabled, NISEnabled, IsTamperProtected, AMRunningMode, engine/signature platform+version, signature last-updated time, quick/full scan ages, and the preference values that describe protection posture (PUAProtection, MAPSReporting, SubmitSamplesConsent, CloudBlockLevel, EnableNetworkProtection, EnableControlledFolderAccess, DisableRealtimeMonitoring state). Exclusion lists are summarised as COUNTS only - paths, process names and extensions are never emitted (they routinely contain usernames and are not needed for a status verdict). Third-party antivirus registration is read from the root\SecurityCenter2 AntiVirusProduct class; the raw ProductState value is reported undecoded because Microsoft does not publish an official decoding table (recorded in uncertainty as an E0 observation, not asserted). Every failure mode is explicit: cmdlet missing (Defender removed / non-Windows host), WMI provider failure (observed HRESULT 0x80041013 on the engineering host), access denied under a non-elevated token - each becomes a statusUnavailable reason plus an uncertainty entry, never a silent 'disabled' claim. The report makes no performance claim and no security-score claim; it reports configuration state only (directive Section 6).
tweaks.defaultState: Information only - Windows default Defender configuration is untouched.
tweaks.proposedState: A read-only Defender status object with per-field values, availability reasons and an uncertainty list.

verify.procedure: The returned object has readOnly=true, a defender.statusRead flag, explicit availability reasons on failure and an uncertainty array; no registry/task/service value is written.

rollback.procedure: Not applicable - read-only diagnostic; no journal entry and no mutation.

originalState.method: Not applicable - the report reads and never writes.

sideEffects: A few seconds of Defender WMI queries; no configuration change.
documentationSource: research/sources/r2-atlasos-revios.md (Defender removal fallout: no AV, no MOTW-era warnings)

tweaks.name: Firewall status & profile report
tweaks.description: Read-only report of Windows Defender Firewall state for the Domain, Private and Public profiles.
tweaks.objective: Prove whether each firewall profile is enabled and how inbound/outbound defaults and logging are configured.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implements Get-Nx14FirewallStatusReport. Enumerates the documented Get-NetFirewallProfile objects and reports, per profile: Enabled, DefaultInboundAction, DefaultOutboundAction, AllowInboundRules, AllowLocalFirewallRules, NotifyOnListen, LogAllowed/LogBlocked/LogMaxSizeKilobytes and the log file path. Derived flags are computed explicitly (allProfilesEnabled, anyProfileDisabled, publicProfileDisabled) so a partial configuration cannot be summarised as 'firewall on'. Registered firewall products are counted from root\SecurityCenter2 FirewallProduct (names only, raw state undecoded). If the NetSecurity module is unavailable the report returns firewall.statusRead=false plus the reason and an uncertainty entry. The function never calls Set-NetFirewallProfile, never adds/removes rules and never touches BFE/mpssvc (never-touch services). Remote Assistance / File-and-Printer-Sharing rule edits seen in reference projects (r2) are explicitly out of scope: NEXTRIX has no firewall-rule mutation surface.
tweaks.defaultState: Information only - firewall configuration is untouched.
tweaks.proposedState: A read-only per-profile firewall status object with derived summary flags.

verify.procedure: The returned object has readOnly=true, one row per profile and explicit statusRead/reason fields on failure.

rollback.procedure: Not applicable - read-only diagnostic; no mutation, no journal entry.

sideEffects: Negligible - profile metadata query only.
documentationSource: research/sources/r2-atlasos-revios.md (Atlas keeps Windows Defender Firewall on and states it has no file to turn it off)

tweaks.name: UAC level configuration
tweaks.description: Sets one of three documented UAC levels, always with EnableLUA=1 and the secure desktop on; UAC can never be disabled by this entry.
tweaks.objective: Let an owner pick a documented, stronger UAC prompt level without ever producing a UAC-off machine.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implements Set-Nx14UacLevel with a pure, testable level map (Get-Nx14UacLevelMap). The map contains exactly the documented Administrator-consent values from Microsoft's UAC settings reference: Default = ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin 5 ('Prompt for consent for non-Windows binaries', the Windows default), AlwaysNotify = 2 ('Prompt for consent on the secure desktop') and CredentialsOnSecureDesktop = 1 ('Prompt for credentials on the secure desktop'). Every level writes EnableLUA=1 and PromptOnSecureDesktop=1. The map structurally cannot emit 0 (elevate without prompting), 3/4 (non-secure-desktop consent/credential prompts) or PromptOnSecureDesktop=0; Get-Nx14UacLevelMap is asserted in the self-test and the registry validator independently bans EnableLUA=0. Three documented values are journalled per level, each through the journal-first pipeline: EnableLUA, ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin and PromptOnSecureDesktop (HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System). EnableInstallerDetection, EnableVirtualization and FilterAdministratorToken are deliberately NOT touched (separate documented behaviours; FilterAdministratorToken changes the built-in Administrator token and is out of scope). If the machine currently has EnableLUA=0, the report exposes that as a security finding and applying any level restores UAC (a security increase) with restartRequired=true; the prior 0 is journalled exactly and remains restorable through NX16-013/016. The documented consequence of PromptOnSecureDesktop=0 (prompts can be drawn over / spoofed) is why that direction is not offered, matching the Atlas reject in r2.
tweaks.defaultState: Windows default: EnableLUA=1, ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin=5, PromptOnSecureDesktop=1 (or the machine owner's current documented level).
tweaks.proposedState: The selected documented level, with EnableLUA=1 and the secure desktop on; exact prior values journaled.

verify.procedure: Each of the three values is re-read through Test-NxConfigurationState after the write; verification failure triggers an immediate best-effort restore of the exact recorded originals and a journaled Failed-RestoredOriginal entry.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-NxRollback restores the journaled EnableLUA/ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin/PromptOnSecureDesktop values (removing values that never existed); only-if-ours divergence is reported, never clobbered. A UAC change needs a restart to take effect fully.

originalState.method: Capture-NxRegistryValue per value (existence, kind, exact value, key existence) journaled before the first write.

sideEffects: Elevation prompts for administrators change according to the selected documented level.
Restoring a disabled UAC requires a reboot before the secure desktop is active again.
Company-managed machines may re-apply their policy after the next policy refresh - the report states this uncertainty.
documentationSource: research/sources/r2-atlasos-revios.md (Atlas requires UAC on; secure-desktop-off honestly documented as spoofable and rejected for NEXTRIX)

tweaks.name: SmartScreen configuration
tweaks.description: Sets the documented Microsoft Defender SmartScreen policy to Warn (default) or Block; SmartScreen can never be turned off by this entry.
tweaks.objective: Offer the documented SmartScreen prompt-strength choice while structurally preventing the SmartScreen-off teardown.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implements Set-Nx14SmartScreen with a pure documented level map (Get-Nx14SmartScreenLevelMap). The mechanism is the documented 'Configure Windows Defender SmartScreen' policy under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\System: EnableSmartScreen=1 plus ShellSmartScreenLevel set to 'Warn' (the documented default) or 'Block' (the stricter documented option). The map has no 'Off' member and no path that writes EnableSmartScreen=0; the legacy Explorer\SmartScreenEnabled value is never written by NEXTRIX (the validator separately bans SmartScreenEnabled='Off', and the Shell policy is the documented Windows 11 mechanism). The report (Get-Nx14SmartScreenStatus) additionally reads the legacy Explorer value so a machine already carrying 'Off' is surfaced as a security finding with the documented Windows Security re-enable path - NEXTRIX reports that state rather than silently rewriting undocumented UI values. App Install Control (ConfigureAppInstallControl) and Edge's own SmartScreen/phishing policies are browser/Store territory and are not touched here; MOTW (SaveZoneInformation) is never modified. Every write goes through the journal-first registry pipeline; verification re-reads both policy values and a mismatch restores the exact original.
tweaks.defaultState: No policy values (policy key typically absent); Windows applies the documented Warn behaviour.
tweaks.proposedState: EnableSmartScreen=1 and ShellSmartScreenLevel=Warn or Block (String), exact prior values journaled.

verify.procedure: EnableSmartScreen (DWord 1) and ShellSmartScreenLevel (String Warn|Block) are re-read after the write; a failure restores the exact recorded originals and journals Failed-RestoredOriginal.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-NxRollback restores the journaled policy values exactly (values that never existed are deleted, returning the machine to the documented default).

originalState.method: Capture-NxRegistryValue for EnableSmartScreen and ShellSmartScreenLevel, plus the legacy Explorer SmartScreenEnabled state recorded read-only in the report (never written).

sideEffects: Policy-managed machines show the policy as set by NEXTRIX until rollback or policy refresh.
Block is stricter than the Windows default and may surprise users with legitimate downloads; it is the owner's explicit documented choice.
No effect on browser-level SmartScreen settings, which are owned by the browser configuration category.

tweaks.name: Secure Boot status report
tweaks.description: Read-only Secure Boot status via Confirm-SecureBootUEFI with explicit unsupported/legacy-firmware handling.
tweaks.objective: Report the firmware-measured Secure Boot state without changing firmware or BCD configuration.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implements Get-Nx14SecureBootStatus. Primary query is the documented Confirm-SecureBootUEFI cmdlet (SecureBoot module). On legacy-BIOS or unsupported platforms that cmdlet throws by design; NEXTRIX catches it and returns secureBootEnabled=$null with supported=false and the exact reason, never a guessed False. Firmware type is read via the documented Get-ComputerInfo BiosFirmwareType property (Uefi/Bios) and reported as context. A registry cross-check (HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecureBoot\State UEFISecureBootEnabled) is included only when that key exists and is labeled as a cross-check observation (E0 provenance) - the cmdlet result is authoritative. The report never calls Set-SecureBootUEFI, never clears Secure Boot keys and never writes BCD (NX17 owns BCD; firmware changes are outside NEXTRIX entirely). Secure Boot is on the directive's never-auto-disable list, so this entry has no mutation surface at all.
tweaks.proposedState: Read-only Secure Boot verdict (True/False) or an explicit unsupported/unknown result with reason.

verify.procedure: The report carries readOnly=true, supported, secureBootEnabled and firmwareType; unsupported hardware yields a reason, not a fabricated boolean.

rollback.procedure: Not applicable - read-only; Secure Boot is on the never-disable list.

sideEffects: None (read-only).

tweaks.name: TPM status report
tweaks.description: Read-only TPM presence, readiness and ownership report via Get-Tpm.
tweaks.objective: Give BitLocker/Windows Hello/Credential Guard decisions a factual TPM baseline without initialising or owning anything.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implements Get-Nx14TpmStatus using the documented Get-Tpm cmdlet. Reports TpmPresent, TpmReady, TpmEnabled, TpmActivated, TpmOwned, LockedOut, AutoProvisioning, ManagedAuthLevel, manufacturer id text (control characters stripped - the raw value on the engineering host was 'AMD\0'), manufacturer version, spec version and lockout counters when exposed. The function NEVER calls Initialize-Tpm, Clear-Tpm, Set-TpmOwnerAuth or any provisioning cmdlet: taking ownership or clearing a TPM is irreversible for sealed keys and is outside a tweak playbook's remit. If the TrustedPlatformModule module is unavailable or access is denied, the report returns present=$null with an explicit reason and uncertainty entry. BitLocker/Windows Hello implications are reported as context only, never as a recommendation to change TPM state.
tweaks.proposedState: Read-only TPM status object with per-field availability honesty.

verify.procedure: The report carries readOnly=true and a statusRead flag; unsupported/denied cases carry a reason (never present=false fabrication).

rollback.procedure: Not applicable - read-only; no TPM provisioning command exists in NEXTRIX.

sideEffects: None (read-only).

tweaks.name: VBS / HVCI status report
tweaks.description: Read-only virtualization-based security, HVCI and Device Guard service report from the documented Win32_DeviceGuard CIM class.
tweaks.objective: Report the real VBS/HVCI state (configured vs running) instead of assuming that a registry value equals effective protection.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implements Get-Nx14DeviceGuardStatus. Queries root\Microsoft\Windows\DeviceGuard Win32_DeviceGuard and reports VirtualizationBasedSecurityStatus (0 not enabled, 1 enabled but not running, 2 running), SecurityServicesConfigured, SecurityServicesRunning (documented service IDs: 1 Credential Guard, 2 hypervisor-enforced code integrity, 3 System Guard Secure Launch, 4 SMM firmware measurement), AvailableSecurityProperties and RequiredSecurityProperties, plus CodeIntegrityPolicyEnforcementStatus. Each ID is mapped to a name and the report distinguishes configured-but-not-running from running - the exact distinction ReviOS #222 missed on UEFI-locked Secured-core machines (r2): a write can silently no-op, so NEXTRIX reports evidence and never claims success from a registry read alone. The HVCI registry value (HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\DeviceGuard\Scenarios\HypervisorEnforcedCodeIntegrity Enabled) and the VBS 'Locked' value are reported as secondary observations with explicit provenance. AvailableSecurityProperties decoding is enumerated with the documented property list; when the list does not contain HVCI/hypervisor support the report says so as a capability finding rather than an error. Read-only: no registry write, no bcdedit call, no service change.
tweaks.proposedState: Read-only VBS/HVCI/Device Guard report with configured-vs-running distinction and capability list.

verify.procedure: The report carries readOnly=true, vbsStatus text, configured/running service name arrays and an uncertainty list; a missing CIM class yields supported=false with the reason.

sideEffects: None (read-only).
documentationSource: research/sources/r2-atlasos-revios.md (unconditional VBS/HVCI disable; #222 UEFI-locked silent no-op)

tweaks.name: Memory Integrity consent-gated configuration
tweaks.description: Enables Memory Integrity (HVCI) only with ExplicitConsent and a recorded driver-compatibility review; refuses on unsupported, UEFI-locked, policy-managed or driver-blocked systems. Never disables it.
tweaks.objective: Provide a journaled, prerequisite-checked path to turn Memory Integrity on, and a truthful report for machines where it cannot safely be turned on.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Two functions. Get-Nx14MemoryIntegrityStatus (read-only) reports the HVCI registry value, the Win32_DeviceGuard configured/running services, VBS availability, the DeviceGuard policy values that would override a local write (EnableVirtualizationBasedSecurity, HypervisorEnforcedCodeIntegrity, LsaCfgFlags), the VBS 'Locked' flag and recent CodeIntegrity operational block events (bounded, default 10) as a compatibility heuristic. Set-Nx14MemoryIntegrity (apply action) accepts only mode=Enable and requires BOTH -Approved and -DriverCompatibilityReviewed; the registry entry declares that review parameter as an ExplicitConsent artifact (ADVANCED, ExplicitConsent, presetExcluded). Before writing anything it refuses on: VBS not reported available; VBS UEFI-locked (writes silently no-op on Secured-core - r2 #222); DeviceGuard policy management present (change the policy source, not the local key); one or more observed CodeIntegrity HVCI block events (resolve the driver first - the authoritative incompatible-driver list is Windows Security > Device security > Core isolation, which is not publicly readable via a documented API, hence the recorded review); or missing review consent. The only registry target is HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\DeviceGuard\Scenarios\HypervisorEnforcedCodeIntegrity :: Enabled = 1 (DWord), captured exactly and written through the journal-first pipeline with a code-level banned-target guard that makes an Enabled=0 write impossible (schema.json bans HVCI off without ExplicitConsent; NX14 does not implement the disable direction at all). Verification reads the value back and reports Verified-RestartPending when the value is 1 but the service is not yet running - it never claims effective protection before the reboot. Trade-offs are stated in the entry and returned by the function: some drivers and anti-cheat/DRM components may refuse to load with HVCI on; a reboot is required; reversal is a manual, documented Windows Security action (or NX16 rollback of the journaled prior value), never an automated disable. No performance effect is claimed in either direction.
tweaks.defaultState: Machine-dependent: HVCI may be on, off, policy-managed or unavailable; the report states which.
tweaks.proposedState: HVCI Enabled=1 (DWord) with the exact prior value journaled, restart pending, and a recorded compatibility review.

verify.procedure: The Enabled value is re-read after the write; a read-back of 1 yields Verified-RestartPending and the report re-reads Win32_DeviceGuard after the reboot to confirm the service is running. A failed write or read-back restores the exact journaled original and journals the failure.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-NxRollback restores the journaled prior Enabled value exactly (including deleting a value that never existed). Restoring an off state is a deliberate rollback of NEXTRIX's own change, not an automated security reduction, and requires a reboot.

originalState.method: Capture-NxRegistryValue for the single HVCI target plus a read-only DeviceGuard/policy snapshot and the compatibility-review flag, all recorded in the apply journal entry before the write.

sideEffects: A restart is required before Memory Integrity is effective.
Drivers or anti-cheat/DRM components that do not meet HVCI requirements may fail to load once HVCI is on - this is why the entry is ADVANCED and consent-gated.
No performance benefit or cost is claimed; NEXTRIX makes no performance claim for security features.
UEFI-locked or policy-managed machines are refused with an explanation instead of a silent no-op.
documentationSource: research/sources/r2-atlasos-revios.md (ReviOS unconditional HVCI disable; issue #222 UEFI-lock silent no-op)

tweaks.name: Credential Guard status report
tweaks.description: Read-only Credential Guard configured/running report with the documented policy values that govern it.
tweaks.objective: Report whether Credential Guard is actually running, without reading or touching any credential material.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implements Get-Nx14CredentialGuardStatus. Runtime evidence comes from Win32_DeviceGuard SecurityServicesConfigured/SecurityServicesRunning service ID 1; policy context comes from the documented LsaCfgFlags value under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\DeviceGuard (0 disabled, 1 enabled with UEFI lock, 2 enabled without lock) and the per-boot HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\LSA LsaCfgFlags observation. The report distinguishes 'running', 'configured but not running', 'not configured' and 'policy disabled', and flags mismatches (policy says enabled, runtime not running) as uncertainty rather than success. On Windows 11 Enterprise, Credential Guard may be enabled by default without an explicit policy value; the report says 'running (no explicit policy observed)' instead of claiming a configuration source it cannot prove. The function never reads credential data, never reads LSA secrets, never exports certificates and never changes LsaCfgFlags - the entry is read-only by design and Credential Guard is on the never-auto-disable list.
tweaks.proposedState: Read-only Credential Guard status with policy/runtime reconciliation.

verify.procedure: The report has readOnly=true, configured/running booleans, the policy value text and an uncertainty list; no credential material or secret is read.

sideEffects: None (read-only; no credential or secret access).

tweaks.name: Controlled Folder Access configuration
tweaks.description: Enables or audits Controlled Folder Access and manages the per-app allow-list; turning CFA off is deliberately not implemented.
tweaks.objective: Let an owner turn ransomware folder protection on (or into audit mode) and unblock a legitimate app explicitly, with the exact prior preference and allow-list journaled.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implements Set-Nx14ControlledFolderAccess and Get-Nx14ControlledFolderAccessStatus using the documented Set-MpPreference/Add-MpPreference/Remove-MpPreference -EnableControlledFolderAccess values (0 disabled, 1 enabled/block, 2 audit) and -ControlledFolderAccessAllowedApplications. The accepted modes are Enabled (1) and Audit (2) only: the catalogue's 'On/Off' is realised as On (block) and On-in-audit, because a CONDITIONAL entry may not lower protection (directive Section 15). Disabling CFA entirely is not a NEXTRIX action; the JSON documents that deliberately. Before any change the function captures a 'defenderPreference' descriptor: current mode, the complete allowed-applications array and the protected-folders array (configuration state required for exact restore; no credential or secret is read). Journal-first, then the preference write, then a re-read; a verification failure restores the captured mode and allow-list and journals Failed-RestoredOriginal. Per-app changes are additive/removal by exact path only: wildcards, relative paths and non-existent files are refused before the journal write, and each path is validated with Test-Path -PathType Leaf. 'Audit' records would-be blocks in the Defender event log without blocking - it is offered for owners evaluating compatibility, not as a silent default. The mode is machine-wide and requires Defender to be the active antivirus; when Get-MpPreference is unavailable (third-party AV or a broken provider) the report says so and the mutating path refuses. Rollback (Invoke-Nx14Rollback) restores the mode and allow-list exactly, only-if-ours.
tweaks.defaultState: Windows/Defender default: Controlled Folder Access off (0) on consumer installs unless the owner enabled it.
tweaks.proposedState: EnableControlledFolderAccess=1 or 2 with the owner-selected allowed-app additions/removals; prior mode and lists journaled.

verify.procedure: The preference is re-read after the change: mode equals the requested value and the allow-list contains every add and none of the removals. A mismatch restores the captured mode/list and journals Failed-RestoredOriginal.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-Nx14Rollback (delegated targetType 'defenderPreference') restores the journaled mode and allowed-app list only-if-ours; a mode or list changed by someone else afterwards is reported diverged and left untouched.

originalState.method: Read the complete CFA preference (mode, allowed applications, protected folders) into a 'defenderPreference' journal descriptor before the first write.

sideEffects: Apps the owner has not allowed can no longer write to protected folders (Documents, Pictures, Desktop, etc.) - the documented CFA behaviour; the allow-list is the remedy.
Audit mode does not block; it only records would-be blocks in the Defender event log.
Requires Defender to be the active antivirus; third-party AV setups are refused with an explanation.
NEXTRIX never turns CFA off, so a rollback restores the pre-NEXTRIX state rather than disabling protection by design.

tweaks.name: Exploit Protection report & selective policy
tweaks.description: Read-only system-wide exploit-mitigation report by default; opt-in, per-process mitigation increases with per-item ExplicitConsent. System-wide mitigation masks are never written.
tweaks.objective: Show the real mitigation posture and allow a narrowly scoped hardening of one named application without ever weakening a mitigation.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Default apply action is Get-Nx14ExploitProtectionReport (read-only): it reads Get-ProcessMitigation -System and summarises documented families (DEP, ASLR ForceRelocateImages/BottomUp/HighEntropy, CFG, StrictHandle, SEHOP, ExtensionPoint, ImageLoad, DynamicCode, ChildProcess, Control-flow guard strict mode) with an explicit tri-state mapping (On / Off / Not configured). The numeric cmdlet encoding (0/1/2) is an observation from build 26100, not a published contract, so it is labeled E0-in-output while the entry's evidence stays E1 for the documented cmdlets themselves. It also reports which IFEO keys carry a MitigationOptions value (names only, bounded), so per-process configuration is visible. The opt-in mutating path (Set-Nx14MitigationPolicy) is intentionally NOT the default apply action: it requires -Approved, ExplicitConsent at registry level, a named process and an allow-list of security-increasing mitigations (CFG, SEHOP, ForceRelocateImages, BlockRemoteImageLoads, DisableExtensionPoints, StrictHandle). It refuses wildcards/relative names, refuses to touch a mitigation that is already explicitly ON, refuses to act when the live value is explicitly OFF (no fighting an administrator's decision), records a full Get-ProcessMitigation JSON snapshot under <JournalRoot>\mitigation-exports before the write, journals a 'processMitigation' descriptor with the exact per-mitigation tri-state, applies only -Enable, then re-reads. There is no disable action anywhere: system-wide mitigation masks (kernel MitigationOptions / FeatureSettingsOverride) are on the schema banned list and are never written by NX14 (they remain NX17 troubleshooting territory with ExplicitConsent). Rollback removes only the mitigations NEXTRIX enabled, restoring the captured per-process configuration.
tweaks.defaultState: Information only - the default action reports the mitigation posture and writes nothing.
tweaks.proposedState: A read-only mitigation report, or (opt-in) one named process with owner-selected mitigations enabled and the exact prior per-process state journaled.

verify.procedure: The report carries readOnly=true and per-family rows; the opt-in path re-reads each selected mitigation after the write and journals Verified only when every value equals the intended setting.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-Nx14Rollback (delegated targetType 'processMitigation') removes only the mitigations this entry enabled, or re-applies the captured prior explicit values; a value changed by someone else is reported diverged. The pre-change JSON snapshot is the manual restore artifact.

originalState.method: Get-ProcessMitigation -Name <process> captured before the write (tri-state per mitigation) plus a full JSON snapshot under <JournalRoot>\mitigation-exports; 'not configured' is recorded as such, never guessed as Off.

sideEffects: Per-process mitigations can break an application that relies on dynamic code or unsupported control-flow patterns - hence per-item consent and no defaults.
Mitigations apply to newly started processes; running instances keep their current configuration until restarted.
No performance claim is made for any mitigation setting.
System-wide mitigation masks are never modified by NX14.
documentationSource: research/sources/r2-atlasos-revios.md (system-wide mitigation nuking rejected; mitigations-off can trigger anti-cheat)

tweaks.name: BitLocker status report
tweaks.description: Read-only BitLocker volume and key-protector-type report - never reads or prints recovery passwords or key IDs.
tweaks.objective: Report encryption protection state honestly while guaranteeing that no recovery secret enters the journal, logs or support bundle.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implements Get-Nx14BitLockerStatus via the documented Get-BitLockerVolume cmdlet. Per volume it reports MountPoint, VolumeType, ProtectionStatus, LockStatus, EncryptionPercentage, EncryptionMethod, AutoUnlockEnabled, and the SET OF KEY-PROTECTOR TYPES (Tpm, TpmPin, TpmStartupKey, NumericalPassword, RecoveryPassword, ExternalKey, Certificate, Password, Unknown). KeyProtectorId values, recovery passwords and external key material are never read into the output object, never written to the journal and never included in a report; the function deliberately projects only the type name. If the BitLocker module is unavailable (edition or role not present) the report returns statusRead=false with the reason and an uncertainty entry rather than inferring from WMI. `manage-bde -status` is not shelled out: its output is locale-dependent and can include key identifiers, so the cmdlet is the only source. The report is explicit that protection state is not proof of a backed-up recovery key - NEXTRIX does not manage, escrow or display recovery keys, and the JSON says so. BitLocker is on the never-auto-disable list; the banned PreventDeviceEncryption=1 pattern is not present anywhere in NX14.
tweaks.proposedState: Read-only per-volume BitLocker status with protector types and no key material.

verify.procedure: The report has readOnly=true, one row per volume, protector TYPE names only, and no property containing a password, key ID or key material.

rollback.procedure: Not applicable - read-only; NEXTRIX never disables, suspends or re-keys BitLocker.

sideEffects: None beyond metadata queries; no secret is read or emitted.

tweaks.name: Windows Sandbox provisioning
tweaks.description: Provisions the documented Windows Sandbox optional feature, with edition, virtualization and restart handling; the exact prior feature state is journaled.
tweaks.objective: Give an owner a disposable-isolation environment through the documented feature mechanism, without hidden downloads or third-party software.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implements Get-Nx14WindowsSandboxStatus and Set-Nx14WindowsSandbox. The feature is the documented Containers-DisposableClientVM optional component (Windows Sandbox requires Windows 11 Pro/Enterprise/Education, firmware virtualization and SLAT; the Microsoft Sandbox page states the prerequisites). The function reads the feature state, edition id and virtualization facts (Win32_ComputerSystem HypervisorPresent, Win32_Processor VirtualizationFirmwareEnabled, SLAT support), then refuses Enable on unsupported editions or when firmware virtualization is absent - instead of queueing a feature that cannot work. The state change reuses NX01-015's verified optional-feature pipeline (Set-NxOptionalFeatureState) when that module is loaded and falls back to the same documented Enable/Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -NoRestart pipeline locally, so there is exactly one mechanism. The prior feature state (Enabled/Disabled/EnablePending) is journaled before the change, the restart requirement is surfaced (Reboot) and pending states are reported as Verified-RestartPending rather than success. Warnings returned by the function: Windows Sandbox and third-party hypervisors (VMware/VirtualBox) can conflict; nested virtualization inside a VM is not supported; enabling/disabling features changes the servicing footprint. No download, no ISO, no third-party binary is involved. Rollback restores the journaled prior feature state.
tweaks.defaultState: Windows default on supported editions: Containers-DisposableClientVM disabled until the owner enables it.
tweaks.proposedState: Containers-DisposableClientVM Enabled (pending restart); prior state journaled.

verify.procedure: The feature is re-read after the change; Enabled or EnablePending yields Verified/Verified-RestartPending, and the ownership/edition refusal paths return an explicit unsupported reason.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-Nx14Rollback (delegated targetType 'optionalFeature'/'feature') restores the journaled prior feature state through the same documented pipeline only-if-ours; a state changed by someone else is reported diverged.

originalState.method: Get-WindowsOptionalFeature state captured and journaled before the change (Enabled/Disabled/Pending are preserved verbatim).

sideEffects: A restart is required before Windows Sandbox is usable.
Enabling the feature adds its servicing footprint; disabling an in-use Sandbox feature requires the Sandbox to be closed.
Third-party hypervisors can conflict with the Windows hypervisor stack; nested virtualization inside a VM is unsupported.

tweaks.name: Hyper-V / virtualization platform configuration
tweaks.description: Reports the Hyper-V/VirtualMachinePlatform/HypervisorPlatform feature state and provides an ExplicitConsent-gated toggle with mandatory WSL2/Docker/Sandbox dependency warnings.
tweaks.objective: Make virtualization-platform changes deliberate: show the dependencies first, require explicit consent, and never silently break WSL2, Docker or Sandbox.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Default apply action is Get-Nx14VirtualizationPlatformStatus (read-only): it reports the state of Microsoft-Hyper-V-All, VirtualMachinePlatform, HypervisorPlatform, Microsoft-Windows-Subsystem-Linux and Containers-DisposableClientVM, the hypervisor-present fact, and detected consumers (wsl.exe presence, com.docker.service, vmcompute, Windows Sandbox). It then emits dependency findings: WSL2 requires VirtualMachinePlatform plus the WSL feature/Store package; Docker Desktop requires VirtualMachinePlatform or Hyper-V; Windows Sandbox requires Containers-DisposableClientVM. The mutating path (Set-Nx14VirtualizationPlatform) is opt-in, registry-ADVANCED/ExplicitConsent, and accepts one component per call (HyperV | VirtualMachinePlatform | HypervisorPlatform) with State Enabled|Disabled. Disabling requires BOTH -Approved and -AcknowledgeDependencyImpact and refuses when consumers are detected unless the acknowledgement is present; enabling on Home is refused when the feature is absent (Hyper-V is a Pro/Enterprise/Education capability). The state change reuses the NX01-015 optional-feature pipeline (same documented mechanism, one implementation). Mandatory warnings returned and documented: stopping/disabling virtualization features breaks WSL2, Docker Desktop, Windows Sandbox and any running VMs; enabling Hyper-V changes the hypervisor launch environment and can affect anti-cheat software and third-party hypervisors - re-check NX14-007/VBS state after the restart. The entry makes no performance claim in either direction (the ReviOS 'VBS improves gaming performance' style assertion is explicitly not repeated). BCD is never touched (NX17 owns it). Rollback restores the journaled prior feature state.
tweaks.defaultState: Machine-dependent; on a clean Windows 11 Pro install the optional virtualization features are disabled until enabled by the owner or by WSL2/Docker setup.
tweaks.proposedState: The selected component in the requested state; prior feature state journaled, restart pending, dependency impact acknowledged.

verify.procedure: The read-only report lists each component state and detected consumers; the opt-in path re-reads the feature after the change and treats Enabled/EnablePending (or Disabled/DisablePending) as verified restart-pending states.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-Nx14Rollback (delegated targetType 'optionalFeature'/'feature') restores the journaled prior feature state only-if-ours. A consumer that appeared after the change is reported as context, never silently removed.

originalState.method: Get-WindowsOptionalFeature state for the selected component captured and journaled before the change; the consumer report is captured read-only as context.

sideEffects: Disabling Hyper-V/VirtualMachinePlatform breaks WSL2, Docker Desktop, Windows Sandbox and any running VM - the mandatory dependency warning exists for this reason.
Enabling Hyper-V changes the hypervisor launch environment; anti-cheat software and third-party hypervisors can be affected.
A restart is required for either direction.
No performance claim is made for enabling or disabling virtualization features.
documentationSource: PROFILE_MATRIX.md (P7: Hyper-V/WSL/virtualization features preserved by default - conflict resolution never silently applies)

tweaks.name: Windows Security health aggregate report
tweaks.description: Read-only aggregate of the NX14 status reports (Defender, Firewall, Secure Boot, TPM, VBS/HVCI, Credential Guard, CFA, BitLocker, UAC, SmartScreen) with merged uncertainty and no security score.
tweaks.objective: One truthful overview that feeds every profile and the support bundle, without inventing a security rating.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implements Get-Nx14SecurityHealthReport. It calls the individual read-only NX14 report functions inside isolated try/catch blocks (a failing provider degrades one area, never the whole report), normalises them into area rows {area, status, summary, detail}, and merges every child uncertainty entry with an area prefix. Status vocabulary is fixed and factual: On / Off / Partial / Configured / NotConfigured / Unsupported / Unknown. Derived counts (areasReportingOn, areasReportingOff, areasUnavailable) are plain counts; the report explicitly states that it is NOT a security score and must not be used as one. Coverage and exclusions are declared in the output: no credential material, no BitLocker key IDs or recovery passwords, no Defender exclusion paths, no machine identifiers; BitLocker protection is reported as state only and does not prove recovery-key escrow. Execution is bounded (fixed property sets, no unbounded CIM enumeration) and read-only: no journal entry, no registry/service/task/preference write. Feeds the P9 general-user health view and the NX16-017 support bundle, and is the first thing the coordinator should read when another security entry reports an unexpected state.
tweaks.proposedState: A read-only aggregate report with per-area status, uncertainty and explicit coverage/exclusion statements.

verify.procedure: The report has readOnly=true, one area row per covered report, merged uncertainty, declared coverage/exclusions and an explicit no-security-score statement.

sideEffects: A few seconds of read-only queries across the security providers; one failing provider is isolated to its area.
